engineeringSkip.reason: Extracting usable net energy from quantum vacuum fluctuations is pseudo-science: the Casimir effect produces no net energy gain, and the second law of thermodynamics forbids it.

factCheck.reason: The quantum vacuum is the lowest-energy state of the fields, so its fluctuations cannot be tapped for net power — doing so would violate thermodynamics, and the Casimir effect only exerts a tiny force between nearby surfaces, it does not deliver usable energy.
